episodes.168902: Diurnal heating, along with a weak upper shortwave moving south over the region on the eastern periphery of an upper ridge, and convergence along surface boundaries, led to a cluster of thunderstorms that shifted south over the central Midlands of SC, some of which reached severe limits.
episodes.168918: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze, and one thunderstorm that moved across the Cape in Brevard County produced a couple of strong wind gusts.
episodes.168937: A cyclic supercell developed across central Kansas, during the evening of June 23rd, 2022. A total of 6 tornadoes touched down during the evening. There were winds that overturned a semitrailer and camper on Interstate 70. Additionally up to ping ping ball sized hail fell.
episodes.169222: During the late afternoon, and early evening of Thursday, June 23rd, a small complex of storms developed in central Minnesota. These storms were developing along an 850mb confluent boundary with an above normal plume of PWATs of 1.25. Due to a high freezing level, a sounding profile suggesting efficient warm-rain processes dominated.  With back-building storms across central Minnesota, rainfall amounts were excessive. Some areas received up to 7 inches of rainfall before rates diminished during the pre-dawn hours. The worst areas were across Todd, Morrison, Stearns and Benton Counties where a band of 3 to 6 inches fell before 4 am. In addition to the heavy rainfall, and flash flooding, the initial hazard was isolated large hail.
episodes.169245: A severe thunderstorm developed over north central Todd County and tracked slowly northeast into Mellette County. The storm produced lots of hail around quarter size along with very heavy rain.
episodes.169247: A thunderstorm became severe over northeastern Mellette County and slowly tracked northeast into Jones County. The storm produced large hail northeast of White River.
episodes.169248: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Mellette County, producing large hail in the Wood area, along with heavy rain.
episodes.169350: Abundant monsoon moisture fueled scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. The stronger storms produced gusty winds up to 58 mph across some of the lower valleys of west-central Colorado.
episodes.169454: A weak flow of monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over southern Nevada. One storm produced severe wind.
episodes.169547: Afternoon thunderstorms produce wind damage in Levy County.
episodes.169548: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170224: A surface trough axis moved inland in the afternoon and enhanced convergence across our inland zones as diurnal instability peaked. Scattered strong to severe storms developed across inland NE FL in the afternoon and evening near the westward moving trough axis.
episodes.170231: A weak low pressure system triggered several thunderstorms in a hot and favorable environment across north central South Dakota on the evening of the 23rd. The strongest of these storms produced large hail, ranging from nickel to two inches in diameter.
episodes.170232: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening across central South Dakota, in association with an area of low pressure and cold front in a hot and muggy environment. Large hail was the main hazard, with stones ranging from quarter to tennis ball size. A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms then developed across northeastern South Dakota during the late evening, and these produced straight-line wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.170344: Scattered strong to isolated severe thunderstorms rumbled across portions of this six-county North Central Kansas areas during the late afternoon and evening hours on this Thursday. The most intense storm in the local area impacted Mitchell County, resulting in a few reports of marginally-severe winds and hail up to ping pong ball size. A gust of 59 MPH was measured by a mesonet station six miles west-southwest of Beloit, while a gust of 58 MPH was measured by a mesonet station located near Tipton. Large hail ranging in size from quarters to ping pong balls was also reported near the towns of Tipton and Victor.||Mid-upper level flow across the region was west-southwesterly, with a subtle shortwave disturbance embedded in the mid-levels sparking off thunderstorms over southwestern Kansas by mid-afternoon. At the surface, elongated low pressure was set up over eastern Colorado northward into the Dakotas, with a warm frontal boundary extending east across the northern half of Kansas. The environment was favorable for the development of supercell storms, with deep layer and effective shear near 40 knots and MLCAPE values of at least 2500 J/kg. There was a concern for the potential for tornadoes in the general region, as 0-1km shear values increased with time to near 30 kts, mainly centered over the I-70 corridor just south of this local area. As scattered thunderstorms spread into the area during the late afternoon and early evening hours, the primary tornadic supercell indeed remained barely south of this coverage area, crossing through Russell and Lincoln counties. However, another supercell eventually developed slightly to its north, pushing slowly east through portions of Osborne and Mitchell counties in this local area mainly between 7-10 PM CDT.
episodes.170393: An upper level trough produced widespread showers and thunderstorms across the Midwest. Meanwhile, isolated storms developed behind the primary area of convection while instability remained high and shear was still in place to help organize storms. Most of these remained sub severe, however one storm just south of Des Moines produced up to golf ball sized hail. Later that evening a cold front swept across the area. A few non sever thunderstorms developed along the front, one of which produced a brief funnel cloud in northeast Iowa.
episodes.170562: A thunderstorm became severe as it moved east of the Bighorn Mountain Range.
episodes.170595: A surface trough, draped across the western Sandhills, served as the focal point for thunderstorm development. Storms tracked east into southwestern Nebraska where they became severe. Hail up to golf ball size was reported in western Lincoln and thunderstorm wind gusts approached 70 MPH in Keith county.
episodes.170638: Thunderstorms training across the Iron Mountain/Norway area resulted in two to three inches of rainfall and caused ponding of water and some minor street flooding in the late afternoon/early evening of 24th.
episodes.170880: An isolated storm moved through north-central KS late on 6/23 and caused wind damage in Ottawa County.
episodes.170930: Clear skies through the day with southwesterly flow at the surface lead to rapid heating and moisture advection across the Northland. This lead to the development of thunderstorms during the afternoon hours that were prolific hail producers across the region with the largest hail bring the size of baseballs. Additionally, slow storm movement along with training storms near Pine Center produced some flash flooding.
episodes.171020: In the afternoon of June 24th, a single cell thunderstorm formed in eastern Colorado, near the Colorado and Kansas border. This storm split into two with the right section heading slightly north of east into Greely County, KS while the left section moved north-northwest into Cheyenne County, CO.  The Cheyenne County storms produced hail up to nickel size. As these storms began dissipating, a line of thunderstorms formed in northeast Colorado and moved east-northeast. These storms extended from east central Colorado into west central Nebraska. Once the line of developing storms caught up to the remnants of the first storms, the line intensified. Over the next few hours in Colorado these storms produced more nickel sized hail and winds up to 61 mph.
episodes.171021: In the afternoon of June 24th, a single cell thunderstorm formed in eastern Colorado, near the Colorado and Kansas border. This storm split into two with the right section heading slightly north of east into Greely County, KS while the left section moved north-northwest into Cheyenne County, CO. The Greeley County storm produced hail up to penny size. As these storms began dissipating, a line of thunderstorms formed in northeast Colorado and moved east-northeast. These storms extended from east central Colorado into west central Nebraska. Once the line of developing storms caught up to the remnants of the first storms, the line intensified. Over the next few hours in Kansas these storms produced more penny sized hail.
episodes.171060: Strong surface heating and deep moisture led to conditions favorable for severe thunderstorms along an inland moving sea breeze.
episodes.171116: A weak surface front pushing southward across south central Alabama encountered a very warm and unstable air mass.  A few strong to severe storms developed along this boundary.
episodes.171268: A weak short-wave trough moved into the area with thunderstorms developing. A few storms became severe in Ward and Bottineau counties, producing one inch diameter hail and 60 mph wind gusts.
episodes.171269: Thunderstorms formed along and near a warm front draped through central North Dakota during the afternoon and early evening hours, with many becoming severe. Early in the event, a tornado formed over south central Wells County, north of Chaseley. The tornado impacted no structures and so there was no damage to evaluate, so was rated EF Unknown by NWS policy. Heavy rains over northeast Wells County led to flash flooding, with water flowing over County Highway 5. Elsewhere, large hail was the primary threat, though there were also some occurrences of severe wind gusts. The largest hail reported was the size of a golf ball, which occurred in Stutsman County. The highest wind gust was measured at 70 mph in Kidder County.
episodes.171530: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were scattered reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.171536: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were scattered reports of wind damage with the strongest storms.
episodes.171654: Moist southerly winds south of a frontal system over North Florida helped to trigger strong afternoon thunderstorms over the Lake Okeechobee area.
episodes.171766: A sea breeze boundary on the Mississippi coast was the focal point for thunderstorms to develop. As the storms collapsed with loss of daytime heating, they produced a downburst of damaging winds in Jackson County.
episodes.171793: Two rounds of severe thunderstorms produced large hail and gusty winds across the northern Red River Valley and into northwest Minnesota. Hail up to 2.75 inches was reported.
episodes.171794: Two rounds of severe thunderstorms produced large hail and gusty winds across the northern Red River Valley and into northwest Minnesota. Hail up to 2.75 inches was reported.
episodes.171847: Monsoonal moisture resulted in thunderstorms with gusty outflow winds in portions northern Utah, as well as flash flooding in portions of southern Utah.
episodes.171873: Summertime convection produced scattered severe thunderstorms with reports of damaging winds and hail. In addition, pockets of heavy rainfall fell over portions of western and central Georgia, ranging from 2 to 4 inches in a short period of time. Just outside of Byron in Peach County, a single report of flash flooding was received.
